hook: A Range Fouler Reporting Form filed by an O-2 crew member of 1172 ATKS on October 15, 2020, documenting a roughly 74-second infrared sensor contact with a round, thermally cold object over the Gulf of Aden that made abrupt directional changes before disappearing.
why_it_matters: This form represents the standardized military apparatus for capturing UAP contacts during active operations — not training exercises — providing sensor-derived geometry (slant range, ground range, sensor depression angle) alongside behavioral anomalies. The thermal signature is notable: the object appeared bright white in black-hot IR mode, meaning it was cold relative to its surroundings, the inverse of a propulsion-heated craft. The abrupt directional changes at only 20 mph add a maneuverability data point not explained by conventional balloon-drift dynamics.

key_findings.finding: The object was tracked as round and thermally cold in infrared — appearing bright white in black-hot mode — traveling northwest at 319 degrees and approximately 20 mph from an altitude near sea level while the aircraft was at 19,073 feet.

key_findings.finding: Precise sensor geometry was recorded: the ATFLIR was depressed approximately 50 degrees below aircraft altitude, with a slant range of 4.06 NM and a ground range of 4.78 KM, enabling geometric reconstruction of the contact's position.

key_findings.finding: The event occurred during an ISR (Intelligence, Surveillance, Reconnaissance) mission — not a training exercise — placing operational context around the observation and making the airspace intrusion potentially more significant.

key_findings.finding: The report was processed through the SPEAR system, which explicitly sanitizes all identifying information for aircrew and squadron before analysis — indicating an institutionalized anonymization protocol for UAP reports at the time of this filing.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: This standardized Range Fouler form from 2020 is precisely the category of military operator report that AARO was established to collect and analyze under post-2021 UAP disclosure mandates.

MITRE has provided analytical support to DoD UAP programs and the SPEAR data-collection infrastructure represents the kind of standardized reporting architecture MITRE has helped design for the intelligence community.
